questions.question: A block of mass 5 kg lies at rest on a rough horizontal plane with coefficient of friction 3/7. A force of magnitude P N acts at 30 degrees above the horizontal. Given P = 14, find the magnitude of the frictional force and describe what happens to the block.
questions.answer: Friction = 7 sqrt(3) = 12.1 N; the block stays at rest because 12.1 N is less than the limiting friction 18 N.
steps: Vertically: R + 14 sin 30 = 5 x 9.8, so R = 49 - 7 = 42 N.
Limiting friction: F_max = mu R = (3/7)(42) = 18 N.
Horizontally, the applied force component is 14 cos 30 = 7 sqrt(3) = 12.12 N.
12.12 N < 18 N, so the block is in equilibrium and the friction is 12.1 N (7 sqrt(3) N).
The block remains at rest.

questions.question: The block (mass 5 kg, mu = 3/7) on the rough horizontal plane is now on the point of slipping along the plane under a force P N at 30 degrees above the horizontal. Find the value of P.
steps: Vertically: R = 49 - P sin 30 = 49 - P/2.
Limiting friction: F = mu R = (3/7)(49 - P/2) = 21 - 3P/14.
Horizontally, limiting: P cos 30 = F, so (sqrt(3)/2)P = 21 - 3P/14.

questions.question: A parcel of mass 2 kg is pulled up a rough plane inclined at 30 degrees to the horizontal by a constant 18 N force acting at 40 degrees to the plane, in a vertical plane containing a line of greatest slope. The coefficient of friction is 0.3. The parcel is a particle P. Find the acceleration of P.
questions.answer: a = 1.18 m s^-2 up the plane (3 s.f.)
steps: Perpendicular to the plane: R + 18 sin 40 = 2 x 9.8 cos 30, so R = 16.97 - 11.57 = 5.40 N.
Friction (opposing the upward motion): F = 0.3R = 1.62 N, acting down the plane.
Along the plane (up positive): 18 cos 40 - 2 x 9.8 sin 30 - F = 2a.

questions.question: Points A and B lie on a line of greatest slope with AB = 5 m, B above A. P passes A with speed 2 m s^-1 up the plane, with the acceleration found in part (a). Find the speed of P as it passes B.
steps: Use v^2 = u^2 + 2as with u = 2, a = 1.184, s = 5.

questions.question: At B the 18 N force is removed and P comes to rest at C. Determine whether P will remain at rest at C, showing all working.
questions.answer: No: the gravity component 9.8 N exceeds the maximum friction 5.09 N, so P slides back down.
steps: Without the 18 N force, the normal reaction is R = 2 x 9.8 cos 30 = 16.97 N.
Maximum friction (limiting) = mu R = 0.3 x 16.97 = 5.09 N.
Component of weight down the plane = 2 x 9.8 sin 30 = 9.8 N.
Since 9.8 N > 5.09 N, friction cannot hold P, so P will not remain at rest and slides back down the plane.

questions.question: A car of mass 1200 kg tows a trailer of mass 600 kg up a road inclined at alpha to the horizontal, where sin alpha = 1/12. The driving force is 3000 N, the car accelerates at 0.75 m s^-2. Resistances: car 2R N, trailer R N. Show that R = 60.
steps: Whole system (mass 1800 kg), up the road positive: 3000 - 2R - R - 1800 x 9.8 sin alpha = 1800 x 0.75.
R = 60 (shown).

questions.question: Using R = 60, find the tension in the tow bar between the car (1200 kg, driving force 3000 N, resistance 120 N) and the trailer (600 kg, resistance 60 N) on the incline with sin alpha = 1/12.
steps: Trailer, up the road positive: T - 60 - 600 x 9.8 sin alpha = 600 x 0.75.

questions.question: The car and trailer move at 12 m s^-1 when the tow bar breaks. The trailer's resistance stays at R = 60 N, the trailer has mass 600 kg and the road has sin alpha = 1/12. Find the further distance moved by the trailer before it first comes to rest.
steps: After the break the trailer has no driving force; it moves up the slope and decelerates.
Deceleration = 550/600 = 11/12 m s^-2.

questions.question: A fixed rough plane is inclined at theta to the horizontal with tan theta = 5/12. A particle of mass 6 kg is projected up a line of greatest slope with speed 5 m s^-1 from A. The coefficient of friction is 1/4. Find the magnitude of the frictional force acting on the particle as it moves up the plane.
steps: From tan theta = 5/12: sin theta = 5/13 and cos theta = 12/13.
Normal reaction R = 6 x 9.8 x 12/13 = 54.28 N.
Friction F = mu R = (1/4)(54.28) = 13.6 N (3 s.f.), acting down the plane while moving up.

questions.question: The particle (mass 6 kg, projected up the plane from A with speed 5 m s^-1, tan theta = 5/12, mu = 1/4) comes to instantaneous rest at B. Find the distance AB.
steps: Moving up, both gravity component and friction act down the plane.
Gravity component = 6 x 9.8 x 5/13 = 22.62 N; friction = 13.57 N.

questions.question: The particle slides down from B and passes through C on the plane with speed again 5 m s^-1. The particle has mass 6 kg, tan theta = 5/12 and mu = 1/4. Find the distance BC.
steps: Moving down the plane, gravity component (22.62 N) acts down and friction (13.57 N) acts up the plane.
Net force down the plane = 22.62 - 13.57 = 9.05 N, so a = 9.05/6 = 1.51 m s^-2.
Using v^2 = 2as with v = 5: 25 = 2(1.508)(BC).

questions.question: A rough plane is inclined at alpha to the horizontal, where tan alpha = 3/4. A particle P of mass 2 kg is held in equilibrium on the plane by a horizontal force of magnitude X N in a vertical plane containing a line of greatest slope. Show that when X = 14.7 there is no frictional force acting on P.
questions.answer: With X = 14.7, the force component up the plane (0.8 x 14.7 = 11.76 N) equals the weight component (19.6 x 0.6 = 11.76 N), so F = 0.
steps: From tan alpha = 3/4: sin alpha = 3/5 and cos alpha = 4/5.
Along the plane (up positive): X cos alpha - 2 x 9.8 sin alpha + F = 0.
Weight component down the plane: 19.6 x 3/5 = 11.76 N.
Force component up the plane: 14.7 x 4/5 = 11.76 N.
These are equal, so F = 0 (no friction), as required.

questions.question: Particle P (mass 2 kg) on the rough plane (tan alpha = 3/4) is held in equilibrium by a horizontal force X N. With coefficient of friction 0.5, find the smallest possible value of X.
steps: Normal reaction: R = 19.6 x 4/5 + X x 3/5 = 15.68 + 0.6X.
Smallest X: P is about to slide down, so limiting friction 0.5R acts up the plane.

questions.question: A particle of mass m rests in equilibrium on a fixed rough plane inclined at alpha to the horizontal, tan alpha = 3/4, under a force X acting up a line of greatest slope. The coefficient of friction is mu. When X = 2P the particle is on the point of sliding up the plane; when X = P it is on the point of sliding down. Find mu.
steps: From tan alpha = 3/4: sin alpha = 3/5, cos alpha = 4/5, so R = (4/5)mg.
Sliding up (X = 2P, friction down the plane): 2P = (3/5)mg + mu(4/5)mg.
Sliding down (X = P, friction up the plane): P = (3/5)mg - mu(4/5)mg.
Substitute P into the first: 2[(3/5) - (4/5)mu] = (3/5) + (4/5)mu.
